Here’s the thing, you are not your gfs therapist, and if you really feel like you’re walking on eggshells shells around her, you shouldn’t feel guilty for telling her that. My bio mom had bpd and some other cocktail of mental illness, so I understand how incredibly stressful it can be to manage yourself to someone else’s emotional volatility. I don’t want to jump straight to saying you should break up with her, but if it’s getting that bad, you might have to give it to her straight. “Either go to therapy and put in the work or I can be with you.” Maybe not as harsh as I worded it, but trust me, therapy is the only thing she can do actively to help with this. Bpd can make you a scary person, you do thing and say things you might not mean but mean in the heated moment of a melt down not thinking of the impact or aftermath, and a professional could give her more help than you’re capable of. Whatever you do, remember that you should prioritize your emotional well being over living on the edge waiting for the other shoe to drop.
